Class Site (C : Category) := { covering_family (u : C) := sigT (Vector.t (∃ uᵢ, uᵢ ~> u)); coverage (u : C) : covering_family u; coverage_condition (u : C) (fs : covering_family u) (v : C) (g : v ~> u) : ∃ hs : covering_family v, ForallT (λ '(vⱼ; hⱼ), ExistsT (λ '(uᵢ; fᵢ), ∃ k : vⱼ ~> uᵢ, fᵢ ∘ k ≈ g ∘ hⱼ) (`2 fs)) (`2 hs) }.
Theorem sheaf_iso_closed (X Y : Presheaf C Sets) (iso : X ≅[@Presheaves C Sets] Y) : Sheaf X → Sheaf Y.

statement_record.book: For a topological space (X, Op) and a presheaf P : Op^op → Set, and a family (U_i)_{i∈I} of opens covering U: a MATCHING FAMILY is a tuple (s_i ∈ P(U_i))_{i∈I} with s_i|_{U_i ∩ U_j} = s_j|_{U_i ∩ U_j} for all i, j; a GLUING is s ∈ P(U) with s|_{U_i} = s_i for all i; P satisfies the SHEAF CONDITION for the cover when every matching family has a UNIQUE gluing, and P is a SHEAF when this holds for every open cover. A morphism of sheaves is a morphism of underlying presheaves (a natural transformation), giving the category Shv(X, Op).
statement_record.intree: Class Sheaf `{@Site C} (X : Presheaf C Sets) := { restriction : ∀ u : C, let '(i; f) := coverage u in ForallT (λ '(uᵢ; fᵢ), ∀ xᵢ : X uᵢ, (∀ (v : C) (g : v ~> uᵢ), ForallT (λ '(uⱼ; fⱼ), ∀ h : v ~> uⱼ, fᵢ ∘ g ≈ fⱼ ∘ h → ∀ xⱼ : X uⱼ, fmap[X] g xᵢ ≈ fmap[X] h xⱼ) f) → ∃! x : X u, fmap[X] fᵢ x ≈ xᵢ) f }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker, in three independent ways, two of them serious. (1) THE MATCHING-FAMILY QUANTIFIER IS WRONG. The book quantifies over a whole tuple (s_i)_{i∈I} at once and asks for one x gluing ALL of them; the in-tree [restriction] is per-leg — under the outer [ForallT] each leg uᵢ is handed a SINGLE section xᵢ and produces its own [∃! x, fmap[X] fᵢ x ≈ xᵢ], so no simultaneous matching family and no simultaneous gluing is ever formed. (2) THE COMPATIBILITY ANTECEDENT IS TOO STRONG, HENCE THE WHOLE CONDITION IS VACUOUS BEYOND SUBSINGLETONS. The inner hypothesis quantifies over ALL xⱼ : X uⱼ rather than over the given sections of a fixed family; Theory/Sheaf/Category.v:28-42 records the instantiation v := uᵢ, g := h := id, j := i, which forces xᵢ ≈ xⱼ for EVERY xⱼ : X uᵢ, so the antecedent is satisfiable only when X uᵢ is a subsingleton and the condition says nothing at any covered object with two inequivalent sections. (3) A SITE CARRIES ONE COVER PER OBJECT, not a collection: [coverage u : covering_family u] is a single vector-indexed family, so 'for every open cover' is replaced by 'for the chosen cover', as Theory/Sheaf.v:164-166 discloses. What IS faithful: the presheaf side ([Presheaf U C := U^op ⟶ C], restriction = fmap), the pullback-stability axiom of a coverage, and the category-of-sheaves clause — Sheaves is the FULL subcategory of presheaves on the predicate, so sheaf morphisms are exactly natural transformations (Sheaves_Full + Sheaves_Faithful), matching the book's 'a morphism of sheaves is just a morphism of the underlying presheaves' exactly. Repleteness (sheaf_iso_closed) is an extra the book does not state.

gap: Three precise gaps. (a) NO TOPOLOGICAL SPACES: there is no Top, no topology, no poset-of-opens Op(X) anywhere in the tree (grep -rniE 'topological|open subset|Sierpinski' over *.v returns only bibliographic prose), so the book's site Op(X) is never instantiated and Shv(X, Op) as such does not exist — only Sheaves over an abstract Site. (b) THE SHEAF PREDICATE IS NOT THE BOOK'S: gluing is per-leg rather than over a simultaneous matching family, and the compatibility antecedent is self-contradictory except on subsingleton fibres, so the in-tree Sheaf class is provably vacuous at any covered object with two inequivalent sections; re-founding it on honest matching families is a named deferral (ledger entry 1). (c) A Site picks ONE covering family per object, not a collection, so 'sheaf for every open cover' is not statable. Note also that the vector-indexed cover admits the EMPTY family, for which ForallT is inhabited by ForallT_nil, so the in-tree condition imposes nothing at all for an empty cover (see example7.36).

statement_record.book: Section 7.4 opens by DEFINING a topos to be a category of sheaves. Consequences drawn on the spot: Shv(X, Op) is a topos for every topological space; Set = Shv(pt) is a topos; and for any database schema (finitely presented category) C, the instance category C-Inst is a topos, presheaves counting as sheaves (footnote 10, to be made precise via sites). Footnote 9 records the alternative names sheaf topos / Grothendieck topos, and the more general ELEMENTARY topos of Lawvere.
statement_record.intree: Class ElementaryTopos (C : Category) := { topos_terminal : @Terminal C; topos_cartesian : @Cartesian C; topos_pullbacks : @HasPullbacks C; topos_closed : @Closed C topos_cartesian; topos_classifier : @SubobjectClassifier C topos_terminal }.  — plus Definition Sheaves : Category := Sub (@Presheaves C Sets) Sheaves_sub with Sheaves_Full / Sheaves_Faithful.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker AND differently founded. The library takes the book's FOOTNOTE-9 notion (Lawvere's elementary topos, axiomatized by finite-limit data + cartesian closure + a subobject classifier) as its primitive, and it is genuinely inhabited (FinSet_Topos, whose Pow 2 = 4 by eq_refl). The book's DEFINIENS — 'a topos IS a category of sheaves' — is not in-tree at all: the two halves (the category Sheaves and the class ElementaryTopos) exist in separate files and are never connected. Concretely, none of the book's three consequences is proved: no ElementaryTopos instance on Sheaves C, none on any presheaf category [C^op, Sets] or instance category C-Inst, and none on Sets itself (Structure/Topos.v:107-110 discloses that Sets' classifier survives only as the cross-universe theorems of Instance/Sets/Classifier.v, not as an instance). Neither is the converse bridge (Giraud) present. Independently, the in-tree Sheaf predicate the category Sheaves is cut out by is itself defective (see def7.35), so even a future proof would have to be preceded by re-founding it.

gap: The identification 'topos := category of sheaves' is entirely missing. Specifically: (1) no theorem or instance ElementaryTopos (Sheaves C) — Theory/Sheaf/Category.v proves only that Sheaves is a category with a full, faithful, replete inclusion into presheaves; (2) no theorem that a presheaf category [C^op, Sets] (equivalently the book's instance category C-Inst) is a topos, and no notion of trivial/canonical topology making presheaves sheaves; (3) no Grothendieck-topos definition or Giraud-style characterization; (4) Sets is not an in-tree ElementaryTopos instance, so 'Set is a topos' is available only as the cross-universe classifier theorems of Instance/Sets/Classifier.v (sets_char_pullback, sets_char_unique, sets_char_subobject) plus separately-proved cartesian/closed structure; the only assembled witness is FinSet_Topos. What IS present: the elementary-topos class of the book's footnote 9, with derived power objects Pow a := Ω^a and relations_iso : SubObj (a × b) ≅ (a ~> Pow b), and one computable instance.
